title: KutzInventory export 3.x
description: The JSON that tools/inventory_export.js --format 3 writes (export/inventory.json) and that the Companion uploads to cr0m. Version 3.x omits selected character-profile fields listed below. Since 3.0.0 there are no stats, sheet, talents, spec, role, reputation, statistics, PvP or achievement points, and equipped items are only slotId, id and link. Money is in copper. Times are ISO-8601 UTC strings or null. Objects marked 'open' are copied from the game as-is and may gain keys in any 3.x release; readers must ignore keys they do not know. See schema/README.md for the versioning rules. 3.1.0 adds raids: the cr0m raids tracked with /kinv raid that recorded something. 3.2.0 adds observations: drop, quest and vendor events recorded while enabled (/kinv track; on by default for a new install since addon 1.13.0). Retained events export even after recording is turned off. 3.4.0 adds characters[].crafted: the items the character created, counted as they are made. 3.6.0: quest observations may carry text, the quest's own words as the game showed them. 3.7.0: loot observations may come from a corpse's group-loot roll list (src.via roll, src.threshold), name a boss's encounter (src.encounter), and mark the item the character won by roll (items[].won). Optional characters[].legacyTree added in inventory 2.1.0 / 3.8.0. 3.9.0: trainer observations (a class or profession trainer's list as the game showed it, with costs, spell ids and the trainer's reaction rx); vendor observations may carry rx and filtered. 3.10.0: observations may carry npcs, a cumulative per-install summary of the creatures the player looked at, with install naming the install it summarises. 3.11.0: taxi observations (a flight master's reachable nodes and prices) and flight observations (how long a flight between two nodes took); npcs entries may carry svc, the services an NPC was seen to offer; quest observations may carry lv, group, freq, timed and startItem (accept) and xp and rep (turnin: the reputation changes, never a standing). 3.12.0: gossip and quest-greeting text game-authored readable pages and NPC spoken lines. Quest accepts may carry objective definitions and points of interest on the player's acceptance map.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this format. A reader that knows 3.0 can read any 3.x.

prices.description: Every item a vendor sells or buys that the characters have seen, keyed by item ID. Vendor observations only.

updatedBy.description: Character key that last saw the warband bank.

raids.description: Since 3.1.0 (absent before). The cr0m raids tracked in game with /kinv raid <string> that recorded at least one event, oldest scheduled start first. Account-wide: every character of the uploaded file(s) recorded into these. The addon does not verify the signature; receiving servers must verify authorization independently.

open.description: Open: copied from the game, keys may change between client builds.

item.description: One item stack. id is required; the rest is copied from the game (open).

bag.description: Game bag ID (-1 keyring, 0-5 bags, 6-14 bank tabs, 15-23 warband tabs, guild tab number).

updated.description: Raw from the addon for bags/bank (usually null); ISO time for guild tabs.

vendorBuy.description: What the cheapest vendor seen charges per item.

vendorSell.description: What a vendor pays you per item (the game's sell price).

key.description: Stable character id, unique per export. An existing Name-Realm key stays with its GUID (or the first login for a legacy entry without a GUID). A different GUID uses Name-Surname-Realm, or Name-<guid tail>-Realm without a surname; further collisions append the GUID and, if needed, a number before the realm. Treat this as opaque; never reconstruct it from name and realm.

surname.description: Forever surname. Absent when the character has none.

guid.description: Stable game GUID. Personal identifier: do not show publicly.

recording.description: Optional. What the last save captured (written by exporters that record logout checkpoints).

location.description: Last good location. Exact coordinates: treat as private.

updated.description: Section name -> when it was last read. 3.x leaves out the sections it no longer exports (sheet, stats, talents, reputation, statistics, pvp).

equipped.description: What the character wears, as of the last save: enough to show gear between Battle.net refreshes (the API has the rest as of logout). Closed: name, quality, stats and durability come from the API or the item catalog.

slotId.description: The game's inventory slot (GetInventorySlotInfo): 1 head ... 16 main hand, 17 off hand, 18 ranged.

link.description: The item link as the game gives it (enchant and suffix IDs are inside).

hearth.description: Since 3.5.0: where the Hearthstone is set, the inn's town or district as the game names it (GetBindLocation), recorded by KutzInventory 1.11.0 or later. Absent until the game has said. Treat as private, like location.

crafted.description: Since 3.4.0: the items this character created, counted at each of its own "You create" lines in the loot chat (profession crafts and things like conjured food alike), so an item made and then sold, mailed, used or disenchanted before the next save still counts. Always on from KutzInventory 1.10.0; crafts before `since` are unknown. Absent when nothing has been counted.

since.description: When counting began on this character (the first craft seen by KutzInventory 1.10.0 or later).

total.description: Items created since `since`. Not capped by `items` or `days`.

items.description: Per item, sorted by itemId. If there are more than 5000, the most recently made are kept.

name.description: The item's name from its link, in the client's language.

count.description: Items made (a craft that makes 5 adds 5).

crafts.description: How many times it was made ("You create" lines).

days.description: Items made per day, sorted by date: the newest 120 days on which something was made. The date is the player's local date.

string.description: The raid's string exactly as cr0m issued it: KR1.<CODE>.<instanceId>.<startUnix>.<sig>. CODE is the 6-character join code, instanceId 0 when unknown, startUnix the scheduled start in UTC seconds, sig cr0m's 12-character signature (the addon can't check it).

events.description: In time order. The addon records at most 2000 per raid; two saved files tracking the same raid are merged.

raidEvent.description: One thing the addon saw while the raid was active: from 2 h before its start to 8 h after, in a party or raid group, inside an instance. t is when (UTC). Optional fields are left out when the client did not say.

oneOf.description: Entered the instance (also after leaving it and coming back).

instanceId.description: The instance ID the client reports (GetInstanceInfo), which may differ from the string's (journal vs map IDs).

instanceName.description: The instance's name, in the client's language.

oneOf.description: Left the instance (or the raid's window ended, or the group broke up). t is when the loading screen out started.

encounterName.description: Its name, in the client's language.

groupSize.description: Group size the encounter was scaled to.

oneOf.description: ENCOUNTER_END: a kill (success) or a wipe.

encounterName.description: Its name, in the client's language.

oneOf.description: A loot line (CHAT_MSG_LOOT) for anyone in the group, including bonus rolls.

itemLink.description: The item link as the client printed it.

looter.description: The recording character's stable characters[].key for its own loot; other group members use Name-Realm, else the name as the loot line wrote it.

oneOf.description: The group's members, at each start and after each encounter_end.

members.description: Each member, sorted: the recording character's stable characters[].key, other members as Name-Realm.

observations.description: Since 3.2.0, only when drop tracking recorded something (absent otherwise, and in 3.0.0 / 3.1.0). The events drop tracking recorded (loot, quest, vendor and, since 3.9.0, trainer; since 3.11.0, taxi and flight) (/kinv track; opt-in until KutzInventory 1.13.0, on by default since, /kinv track drops off stops it), from the saved table KutzInventoryObsDB. Since 3.12.0 also game-authored gossip, quest greetings readable pages and lines spoken by identified NPCs. Never gold (no coin loot, quest money or player money), player chat, mail or guild data. Contains character identity and location history; consumers must apply their own access controls. Since 3.10.0 also npcs (with install): a cumulative per-install summary of the creatures the player looked at; a later export from the same install replaces it. Readers must ignore event types and fields they do not know.

addon.description: The KutzInventory version that recorded it ("unknown" when the saved file did not say).

install.description: Since 3.10.0, with npcs: the install the npcs summary belongs to, the saved file's random prefix (the same one the event ids start with). When an export merges several saved files (several game accounts) that hold a summary, their prefixes sorted and joined by +. A summary replaces every earlier one whose install shares a part with it; it is not cryptographic or guaranteed globally unique.

events.description: Oldest first. At most 5000 and about 2 MB of JSON; the addon keeps 30 days. Empty only when the section carries npcs.

npcs.description: Since 3.10.0: the creatures this install's players looked at (target, mouseover, an open vendor / quest / trainer window, a loot corpse), one entry per NPC id, sorted by npc. Cumulative per install: a later export replaces an earlier one with the same install; counts are totals, not deltas. Only creatures no player controls, only outside instances. No GUIDs, no player names, no time finer than a day, no order of sightings. At most 3000 (the most recently seen) and about 1 MB of JSON.

observationWhere.description: Where it happened. Fields the client did not give are left out.

map.description: The map / instance ID: GetInstanceInfo() instanceID.

itype.description: Inside an instance only: GetInstanceInfo() instanceType (party, raid, scenario, pvp, arena, ...).

difficulty.description: Inside an instance only: GetInstanceInfo() difficultyID.

x.description: Outside instances only: map position 0-1, 4 decimal places.

y.description: Outside instances only: map position 0-1, 4 decimal places.

observationWho.description: The recording character's level, class ID and faction, because drops and vendors depend on them, and (since 3.3.0) its own name and surname so cr0m can credit the character that found something. Never anyone else's name, and no realm, guild or GUID.

name.description: Since 3.3.0: the recording character's own given name (UnitName("player")). Never another player's.

surname.description: Since 3.3.0: the recording character's own surname (Forever's GetUnitName adds it), when it has one.

observationLink.description: Since 3.3.0: the item's link cut down to its quality colour, id and name, e.g. |cffa335ee|Hitem:19019|h[Thunderfury, Blessed Blade]|h|r. The id is the item's own. Lets cr0m name an item no database has yet. The rest of the game's link (the player's level, spec, enchants) is never kept.

observationEvent.description: One recorded event. type picks the shape.

oneOf.description: A loot window was opened: one event per loot source in it. Every window counts as an open (a coins-only corpse has items []), so drops / opens is a rate. The same corpse or node opened twice is one event; skinning a corpse is a separate open of kind skin. Coins and currencies are never recorded.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

kind.description: chest = any game object that isn't a herb or ore node; container = an item opened from the bags (src.item); quest = a quest reward container.

npc.description: The creature's NPC ID, from its GUID.

object.description: The game object's ID, from its GUID.

item.description: kind container: the opened item's ID.

guid.description: Creatures and objects only, never a player, a player's pet or an item. Consumers may use it to deduplicate a kill across reports; server handling is outside this schema.

level.description: The creature's level when a unit showed it (the same NPC at two levels is two sources).

via.description: How the source was known: slot = GetLootSourceInfo, target = the dead target when the window opened (no GetLootSourceInfo). roll (since 3.7.0) = not a loot window but the corpse's group-loot roll list (Need / Greed), recorded also when another player opened the corpse: it holds only the items at or above threshold, never coins or anything below it, so it is a partial open. Items a loot window of the same character showed are not repeated in it. Without a guid the corpse was not known (kind other).

encounter.description: Since 3.7.0: the DungeonEncounter id of a boss killed while recording (ENCOUNTER_END), on that boss's loot.

threshold.description: Since 3.7.0, via roll only: the group's loot threshold quality (0 poor ... 4 epic) when the list was rolled; the list is every item of that quality or better.

items.description: The items in the window from this source (empty: nothing but coins, or nothing).

won.description: Since 3.7.0: the recording character won this item by roll (its own "You won" loot line). Absent otherwise; who else won is never recorded.

oneOf.description: A quest was accepted or turned in. rewards only on turnin; never the money. text (since 3.6.0) is the quest's own words. Since 3.11.0: lv, group, freq, timed and startItem only on accept; xp and rep only on turnin; each is left out when the client did not say or the addon was not sure. Since 3.12.0: obj and poi only on accept.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The giver (accept) or ender (turnin), when it is a creature.

object.description: The giver or ender, when it is a game object.

chose.description: The picked choice reward's item ID.

text.description: Since 3.6.0: the quest's text as the game showed it to the recording character, with that character's own name put back to $N. On accept: title, details, objectives. On turnin: title, progress, completion. Recorded once per quest and act while that event is kept, so most repeats carry none. Game text, nothing about the player.

details.description: The description in the window that offers the quest (GetQuestText).

progress.description: What the ender says before the quest is complete (GetProgressText).

completion.description: What the ender says in the reward window (GetRewardText).

lv.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the quest's level as the quest log shows it (C_QuestLog.GetInfo level). On a client that scales quests to the character, the level it showed this character.

group.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the quest log's suggested group size (suggestedGroup), only when 2 or more.

freq.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: a daily or weekly quest (the quest log's frequency, Enum.QuestFrequency Daily or Weekly). Absent for any other quest, or when the client did not say.

timed.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the quest has a time limit (C_QuestLog.GetTimeAllowed above 0 when it was accepted). Absent when it has none or the client did not say: absent is not proof of no timer.

startItem.description: Since 3.11.0, accept only: the item that started the quest (the QUEST_DETAIL questStartItemID), only when the window that offered it showed this very quest.

xp.description: Since 3.11.0, turnin only: the XP the reward window showed (GetRewardXP), as offered to this character (it may include the character's XP bonuses). Only while the character is under the level cap with XP not turned off; never 0.

rep.description: Since 3.11.0, turnin only: the reputation the turn-in changed, as changes, never a standing. Each faction's standing was read when the reward window opened and again about a second after the turn-in; only factions in both reads that changed, sorted by f, each once. What this character received, not the quest's listed reward: with its reputation bonuses and any spill-over to other factions, so the same quest can differ between characters. The Guild faction (1168) and renown factions are left out. Absent when nothing changed, more than 6 changed, or something else could have moved them in between (loot, combat, another reward window or turn-in, more than 5 minutes from the window to the turn-in).

d.description: The change in reputation points this character received (with its reputation bonuses): positive gained, negative lost. Never 0.

obj.description: Quest objective definitions in quest-log order. Player progress and completion status are excluded.

poi.description: Distinct game quest markers for the acceptance UI map. x and y are map percent.

oneOf.description: A vendor window was opened: what was for sale at that moment (not proof of the vendor's full or future stock). Since 3.9.0 read under the window's all-items filter (put back at once); prices are as shown, after any reputation discount (see rx).

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

rx.description: Since 3.9.0: the NPC's reaction to the recording character, UnitReaction("npc", "player"): 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly, 6 honored, 7 revered, 8 exalted. Prices and costs are what the game showed, which already include this character's reputation discount; rx lets a reader tell a list price from a discounted one. Absent when the client did not say.

filtered.description: Since 3.9.0: the merchant window's item filter (this class only) could not be switched to all for the read, so items it hides are missing from this list. Absent when the list was read unfiltered (or the client has no such filter).

price.description: Copper per n, as the vendor shows it (0 when it costs only items or currencies).

cost.description: Item or currency costs per purchase.

limited.description: The vendor's limited stock, or null when unlimited.

oneOf.description: Since 3.9.0: a class or profession trainer's window was opened: every service it lists (all three type filters were switched on for the read and put back after), as this character saw them. The hunter's Beast Training window is never recorded. The same trainer with the same list (st aside) and rx is recorded at most once in 7 days. Costs are game prices, not the player's money.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The trainer's NPC ID, from its GUID (the GUID itself is never kept).

kind.description: profession: C_Trainer.GetTrainerType() is Tradeskills; class: any other trainer but Pet (class trainers, weapon masters and other general trainers).

rx.description: Since 3.9.0: the NPC's reaction to the recording character, UnitReaction("npc", "player"): 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly, 6 honored, 7 revered, 8 exalted. Prices and costs are what the game showed, which already include this character's reputation discount; rx lets a reader tell a list price from a discounted one. Absent when the client did not say.

rows.description: The services in the order the window lists them, headers left out. At most 400.

s.description: The spell ID, from C_TooltipInfo.GetTrainerService (the client has no GetTrainerServiceSpellID). Absent when the client gave none.

name.description: The service's name (GetTrainerServiceInfo), at most 120 bytes.

rank.description: Its sub text, e.g. Rank 4 (profession trainers: Apprentice, Journeyman ...).

lv.description: The character level it needs; absent when none.

skill.description: The skill it needs (GetTrainerServiceSkillReq), e.g. Blacksmithing.

needs.description: Abilities it needs first (GetTrainerServiceAbilityReq), at most 5.

cost.description: Copper, as the trainer shows it to this character (after any reputation discount; see rx). A game price, not the player's money.

st.description: a = available (can be learned now), u = unavailable (not yet), k = known. Not part of the 7-day check.

oneOf.description: Since 3.11.0: a flight master's map was opened (TAXIMAP_OPENED): every node this character can fly to from the flight master's own node, with its price. Node ids come from C_TaxiMap.GetAllTaxiNodes, joined by slot to the window's own slot functions; when the client gives no node ids, the two disagree, there is not exactly one current node, or more than 200 nodes are reachable, nothing is recorded. The same flight master, node, list of nodes and prices and rx is recorded at most once in 7 days. Costs are game prices, not the player's money. No node names, no GUID.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

npc.description: The flight master's NPC ID, from its GUID (the GUID itself is never kept).

node.description: The flight master's own node: the taxi node id (TaxiNodes) the window marks as current.

rx.description: The flight master's reaction to the recording character, UnitReaction("npc", "player"): 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly, 6 honored, 7 revered, 8 exalted. Costs are what the game showed, which already include this character's reputation discount. Absent when the client did not say.

to.description: Every node reachable from node (the window's REACHABLE nodes), sorted by node, each once and never node itself. Nodes the character has not discovered or cannot reach are not listed. Empty when none is reachable yet.

cost.description: Copper, TaxiNodeCost as the window shows it to this character. A game price, not the player's money.

hops.description: How many flight legs the route takes (GetNumRoutes). Absent when the client gave none.

oneOf.description: Since 3.11.0: a flight this character took, from boarding to landing. Started by TakeTaxiNode in a taxi window that was read (the destination), PLAYER_CONTROL_LOST and UnitOnTaxi true; ended by PLAYER_CONTROL_GAINED with UnitOnTaxi false. Recorded only when the landing is known to be at to: the position on the taxi map is by that node (no other node closer), or, when the position could not be read, the next taxi window within 2 minutes is at to. Once per from and to in 30 days. No where: never a position or route trail.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When the flight landed, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

from.description: The taxi node id the flight started at (the flight master's own node).

to.description: The taxi node id it landed at, the one chosen in the window. Never the same as from.

sec.description: Seconds from boarding to landing (GetTime, rounded), as this character flew it. Flights under 5 seconds or over an hour are not recorded.

oneOf.description: Game-authored gossip or quest greeting; exactly one subject. Gossip options and GUIDs are excluded.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

oneOf.description: One page of game-authored readable text. A source ID is optional; mail and authored letters are excluded.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

oneOf.description: Sanitized game dialogue or emote from an identified creature. No speaker GUID or recipient.

id.description: Unique per recording install: a random prefix made once, a dash and a counter. cr0m ignores ids it already stored for that person, so uploading the same file twice is harmless.

t.description: When, from the game's time(): Unix seconds.

b.description: The game build when it was recorded: GetBuildInfo() version.build, e.g. 1.60.1.70888. Left out when the client did not say.

legacyTree.description: Current character Legacy trait ranks and choice entries as applied (changes staged before Apply Changes are not recorded), read without loading Blizzard_LegacySystem. Optional until all three trees are available.

observationNpc.description: Since 3.10.0: what the client showed about one creature, summed over this install's sightings. Fields the client did not give (or kept secret) are left out.

npc.description: The NPC ID, from the creature's GUID (the GUID itself is never kept).

name.description: The creature's name as last seen (UnitName), in the client's language, under the subtitle's rules: never an owner title, anything with an apostrophe-s, the recording character's name, markup or a GUID shape.

lv.description: [min, max] of UnitLevel over the sightings (min <= max). A skull (-1) is never a level.

boss.description: UnitLevel was -1 (a skull) while the creature was a world boss or the player was at the level cap. A skull seen by a lower character is not kept.

ct.description: UnitCreatureType: the client's creature type id (1 Beast, 7 Humanoid, ...), else its localized name (up to 40). Companions (12, Non-combat Pet) are never recorded.

fam.description: UnitCreatureFamily: the client's family id, else its localized name (up to 40). Absent for creatures without a family.

rxA.description: UnitReaction(unit, "player") as last seen by an Alliance character, read only while it was alive and out of combat: 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly .. 8 exalted.

rxH.description: UnitReaction(unit, "player") as last seen by a Horde character, read only while it was alive and out of combat: 1 hated, 4 neutral, 5 friendly .. 8 exalted.

sub.description: The subtitle under its name ("Journeyman Tailor"), from the unit tooltip, only when the tooltip's lines prove it is one (line 1 the unit's name, line 3 the level line, line 2 not); never an owner title ("X's Pet") or anything with an apostrophe-s.

svc.description: Since 3.11.0: the services this NPC was seen to offer, sorted, each once: vendor (a merchant window), repair (that window could repair: CanMerchantRepair), flight (a flight master map), trainer, bank, guildbank, inn (CONFIRM_BINDER or HEARTHSTONE_BOUND while talking to it), auction, stable, battlemaster, spirit (a spirit healer), guild (guild registrar or charter seller), tabard. From PLAYER_INTERACTION_MANAGER_FRAME_SHOW (Enum.PlayerInteractionType, by name) and the windows the addon reads; each counts as a near sighting. A set summed over sightings, never gossip text.

spd.description: Beasts only: main-hand attack speed in hundredths of a second (UnitAttackSpeed), read alive and out of combat; the value seen most often (a tie keeps the one seen first).

day.description: The last day it was seen: whole days since 1970-01-01 (UTC), floor(unix time / 86400). Never a time of day.

cells.description: Where the player stood while within about 10 yards of it (CheckInteractDistance) or with a window open with it, so the player's position stands for the creature's: unordered counts of 1% map squares, sorted by uiMap, cx, cy. At most one count per square per 10 minutes in a session; the 40 most counted squares.

observationLabel.description: Since 3.9.0: a short game label (a spell, rank, skill or ability name) as the game showed it. No UI markup (|), no control characters, and nothing shaped like a GUID.

recordedProse.description: Game prose with line breaks, without UI markup, GUID-shaped strings or other control characters.
